newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Beirut to list on BSE on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Beirut to list on BSE on Friday.

text.p: Lebanon's fast-growing Bank of Beirut will start trading its shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange on April 11, the exchange said on Monday.
It will be the third Lebanese bank to list under a 1996 law allowing banks to trade 30 percent of their shares without prior central bank approval.
It raises to eight the number of companies on the Beirut Stock Exchange, which reopened last year after a shutdown of nearly 13 years due to Lebanon's 1975-90 civil war.

"The Beirut bourse committee accepted on April 3, 1997, the listing of Bank of Beirut's C shares in the bourse's official market. Trading will start as of April 11, 1997," the exchange said in a statement.

Bank of Beirut will list 4,800,000 shares. Its shares were valued at $2.17 each last week in a $10.4 million private placement which was 11 times oversubscribed and raised the bank's capital to between $26 million and $27 million.

The other listed banks are Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce, whose shares have risen to $14.25 since they began trading on December 30 at $11.25, and Banque Audi, which is now quoted at $19.25 after starting at $15 on January 15.
A fourth bank, Byblos Bank, is expected to list its shares in mid-year.

Bank of Beirut ranked 17th among Lebanon's 82 commercial banks in terms of customer deposits and 15th in terms of assets. It has 11 branches in Lebanon and is adding two branches a year and has 164 employees.
